# Changelog

## 0.1.6 — PlayStation SPU instrument (candidate)

- Collect the existing BSD-3-Clause standalone MAME-derived SPU adaptation and pristine upstream sources, preserving all imported bytes, notices and SHA-256 provenance. No MAME framework, BIOS, game files or downloads are needed.
- Add `tetorica::ps1_spu`, `<tetorica/ps1_spu.h>` and the unchanged synchronous `ps1_spu_*` C ABI: 24 ADPCM voices, fixed 44,100 Hz stereo, private 512 KiB RAM, pitch, ADSR and preset reverb. Catalog this instrument separately; the 24 generic chip IDs, 29 chip WASM recipes and two application-audio APIs are unchanged. The aggregate selector now has 32 recipes.
- Add an original-waveform Native fixture, a three-second stereo WAV host, real WASM ABI/Native parity checks, release audit regressions and a sixth WASM CI job. Complete builds provide 24 libraries, 30 CTest entries from 29 fixtures and 22 WAV examples.
- Local 0.1.6 packaging is an unpublished candidate. It does not tag, publish or change any consuming application automatically.

## 0.1.5 — POKEY, CD-DA and MSM5205

- Add the original C11 CD-DA PCM device and MSM5205 raw decoder / PC Engine ADPCM RAM helper, preserving the application core/header/bridge bytes and component notices.
- Expose `tetorica::cdda` and `tetorica::msm5205` through public `<tetorica/cdda.h>` / `<tetorica/msm5205.h>` headers and the unchanged `cdda_pcm_*` / `msm5205_pcm_*` ABIs. Both accept C and C++ callers without an audio device or machine runtime.
- Add two `standalone-audio-wasm` descriptor/raw-WASM recipes, three Native fixtures and an original HuC6280 + MSM5205 + CD-DA WAV host. Catalog these two modules separately under `applicationAudio`; the existing 24 chip IDs and 29 sound-chip WASM artifacts stay unchanged.
- Retain both Analyzer JavaScript references and the licensed upstream ADPCM source references. OKIM6295 remains reference-only. Document source lifetime, nibble/rate/loop timing and the host integration boundary.
- Add a BSD-3-Clause standalone POKEY 4.9 adaptation from the pinned, explicitly licensed libvgm core file; retain its exact upstream source, notices and provenance while omitting unmarked framework/helper files. Native and WASM compile the same four-channel core.
- Add independently owned multi-instance handles, synchronous real read-side I/O, raw mono PCM, deterministic reset, source mute and allocation-free rendering. Two ordinary handles supply dual POKEY; host routing remains explicit.
- Add Native/WASM parity and dual-handle isolation tests, original centered-mono/stereo WAV demonstrations, source-archive build checks and a POKEY WASM CI job. With the application-audio modules, the collection describes 24 chip IDs and 31 WASM recipes; Native builds produce 23 libraries, 29 CTest entries and 21 offline WAV examples.
- Publish sources through the matching `v0.1.5` tag after all five Native and five WASM validation jobs succeed. The published 0.1.4 archive remains unchanged; consumers explicitly adopt the new source snapshot. Local packaging alone does not publish a release.

## 0.1.4 — WonderSwan source and standalone builds

- Include the BSD-3-Clause WonderSwan adaptation and pinned MAME source, preserving the imported source and license bytes. Add the `tetorica::wonderswan` Native library and `<tetorica/wonderswan.hpp>` raw C++ API, four wavetable voices, stereo volume, Noise, Sweep, Voice PCM and owned 16 KiB RAM. Keep the unipolar headphone DAC output unchanged; CPU, DMA, Hyper Voice and Tauri backend integration are outside this SDK target.
- Add the WonderSwan WASM recipe and common build receipts as the twenty-eighth artifact. The SDK build produces the same JS/WASM bytes as the imported reference with Emscripten 6.0.6. Add a standalone synchronous Node ABI smoke for released and independently rebuilt artifacts.
- Add a real-core Native fixture and an original three-second stereo WAV example. Source-archive verification now requires twenty libraries, twenty-five CTest entries, twenty-four fixture executables and nineteen WAV examples. Extend the WASM CI to separate YM2612 and WonderSwan jobs; tagged source publication waits for both and all five Native jobs.

## 0.1.3 — Automatic GitHub Releases

- Publish a source ZIP and `SHA256SUMS` automatically when a matching version tag is pushed, after all five Native validation jobs and the YM2612 WASM job succeed. Use the workflow's built-in token and the GitHub REST API; maintainers only need Git to push the tag.
- Keep the previously pinned 0.1.2 source archive unchanged. This release adds publishing automation and documentation without changing sound-chip cores or APIs.

## 0.1.2 — Independent Sega PSG component

- Separate the original Tetorica Sega PSG implementation into `vendor/tetorica_sega_psg/`, with its own BSD-3-Clause license, copyright/SPDX headers and SMS Power! hardware-documentation credit. Update Native/WASM build paths and component provenance without changing synthesis, APIs or the imported reference binaries. Existing fixed application SDK snapshots remain unchanged until consumers explicitly adopt this release.

## 0.1.1 — Standalone Native targets

- Add the alternative `tetorica::nuked_ym2612` target and public `<tetorica/nuked_ym2612.hpp>` exposing both existing synchronous raw `tetorica_nuked_*` and Native `native_nuked_ym2612_*` ABIs. Preserve vendor, Browser bridge, Native wrapper and policy bytes. Compile the core as C and wrapper as C++, with eight C-provider symbol prefixes and the thread dependency for one-time process-global YM2612 selection. The alternative engine retains LGPL-2.1-or-later terms and adds no chip identifier.
- Add the imported Native Nuked fixture with raw ABI/chunk/envelope/reset and C/C++ allocation auditing, plus a co-link/cold-construction test with regular YM2612 and PSG. Add the original offline Nuked+PSG Genesis WAV example. Source verification now builds nineteen static libraries for twenty-two chip IDs plus one alternative engine, runs twenty-four CTest tests from twenty-three fixture executables and renders eighteen WAV examples; twenty-four aliases include generic OPL and alternative Nuked. Analyzer-only sources remain separate.

- Complete standalone coverage of all 22 cataloged Playground chip IDs with `tetorica::spc` and `<tetorica/spc.hpp>`, preserving the existing `native_spc_*`, `NativeSpcState` and `NativeSpcEvent` ABI. Link the unchanged SPC700 CPU/accurate S-DSP sources and Native wrapper; fixed 32 kHz synthesis uses 128-frame blocks and interpolation to 8–384 kHz output. Retain copied loading, pause/resume, cached source mute, bounded incremental control-side seek, analysis snapshots, DSP-write observation and latched-error/reload semantics. Hosts retain original file bytes for Stop-to-start/absolute seeks and own callback handoff/retirement. No Nintendo IPL, metadata-driven ending/fade, portable save state or audio device is added. Keep LGPL-2.1-or-later core/wrapper/included-header notices separate from the new public forwarder's BSD default; shared vendor, wrapper and WASM bytes remain unchanged.
- Add an SPC fixture and `tetorica_spc_wav <output.wav>`: a full original SPC assembled in memory, whose emulated CPU configures DSP voices, polls timer 0 for a stereo melody/chord, then releases all voices. Original sine/triangle/pulse BRR loops, fixed gain/fades and bounded observer validation need no game data, IPL, external file or device. Source-archive verification builds eighteen static libraries for all twenty-two chip IDs, runs twenty-two CTest tests from twenty-one fixture executables and renders seventeen WAV examples; twenty-three aliases/headers include generic `opl`. The alternative Nuked variant is added separately in this version; Analyzer-only chips remain outside these Native targets.
- Add standalone `tetorica::snes` and `<tetorica/snes.hpp>` exposing the unchanged `native_snes_*` ABI and observational `NativeSnesState`. Link only the accurate S-DSP and existing Native wrapper, without SPC700, IPL or file playback. Preserve eight BRR voices, stereo ADSR/GAIN/noise/pitch modulation/echo, copied 64 KiB RAM, stable owned RAM view, same-frame KON/protected gates, retained Stop, full reset and 32 kHz synthesis interpolated to 8–384 kHz output. The optional timeline borrows caller-validated immutable initial RAM/DSP/events; hosts retain arrays through pause/end and serialize all access. Retain LGPL-2.1-or-later core/wrapper/included-ABI-header notices in the separate target, with the SDK BSD default for the new forwarder/integration; shared sources and WASM bytes remain unchanged.
- Add SNES instrument and extended timeline/RAM CTest entries plus `tetorica_snes_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 instrument host. It generates original sine/triangle/pulse BRR loops, auditions left/right voices and an eight-voice chord with ADSR/direct GAIN, then releases every voice. Correct 32 kHz pitch conversion, disabled echo writes, fixed gain and edge fades require no game ROM, external sample or audio device.
- Add standalone `tetorica::dx7` and `<tetorica/dx7.hpp>` exposing the unchanged `native_dx7_*` ABI. Assemble the 24 shared MSFA files and the same six existing Native overrides under the CMake binary directory, including matching quoted-include headers. Amend only Native `synth_unit.cc` panic to reset each preallocated note in place, clearing feedback history for a clean restart without allocation/free or slot-address changes; ordinary Note On/release/kill behavior, shared vendor sources, wrapper and WASM bytes remain unchanged. Preserve six operators, 32 algorithms, 16 preallocated note slots, copied unpacked voices, identity-scoped live edits, mask-protected released tails, kill buffering, immediate-silence panic and fixed 44.1 kHz synthesis with 8–384 kHz output interpolation. Retain Apache-2.0 core/override/wrapper notices and the public forwarder/integration BSD default; C++17 remains the minimum.
- Add the DX7 offline fixture and `tetorica_dx7_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 host with three original 155-byte six-operator voices, algorithms 1/5/32, a live timbre edit, a chord and explicit slot releases. Mono output is duplicated with fixed gain and edge fades; no SysEx, external voice assets or audio device is required.
- Add standalone `tetorica::pwm` and `<tetorica/pwm.hpp>` exposing the unchanged `native_pwm_*` ABI and observational `NativePwmState`. Preserve the shared 32X FIFO/timer/routing core, Native 23,011,361 Hz duty/gain-1 defaults, clock guards, retained Stop/reset and 64-bit FIFO/latch ownership tags. No SH2, DMA, machine runtime or host scheduler is imported; shared core, Native wrapper and WASM bytes remain unchanged.
- Add primary and additional-tag PWM CTest fixtures covering FIFO/timer/routing, output integration, observation, bounds, Stop/reset, ownership isolation and callback allocation checks. Add `tetorica_32x_wav <output.wav>`: three seconds of 48 kHz stereo PCM16, with left/right PWM-only audition followed by original PWM PCM/percussion plus YM2612/PSG. Cycle 960 uses 959-clock source ticks and midpoint 480; a bounded host feeder keeps original data synchronized to the Native clock, with fixed mix gain and fades.
- Add standalone `tetorica::nes` and `<tetorica/nes.hpp>` exposing the unchanged `native_nes_*` ABI for two pulses, triangle, noise, copied DMC RAM and optional FDS. Compile only the self-contained Native renderer, without duplicate vendor exports; preserve NTSC/PAL selection, clock resampling, nonlinear mix/filters, host-protected gates, mute, retained Stop and full reset. Keep Apache-2.0 AND MIT core notices and the default BSD header/integration license. The target uses C++17 and the supported original Tauri integer/aliasing/floating-point flags.
- Add `tetorica_nes_fds_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example: all five APU sources, an original FDS wave, then all six together at the NTSC clock. Original notes, copied DMC bits and wave RAM need no game ROM, external sample or audio device; mono output is duplicated with fixed gain, pitch checks and fades.
- Add standalone `tetorica::huc6280` and `<tetorica/huc6280.hpp>` exposing the unchanged `native_huc6280_*` ABI: six audible wavetable/DDA sources, channel-4/5 noise, LFO, copied 32-sample unsigned 5-bit wave RAM, stereo balance, mute and observational state. Preserve selection, waveform-helper phase effects, retained DDA/Stop and clock/reset behavior. Compile only the wrapper translation unit, including its existing vendor `.cpp`; vendor, Native wrapper and WASM bytes remain unchanged.
- Add `tetorica_pcengine_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example using original wavetable notes, host-fed DDA and both noise sources at 3,579,545 Hz, with deliberate left/right phrases, fixed gain and fades. No device, external assets or ROM is required.
- Add standalone `tetorica::gameboy` and `<tetorica/gameboy.hpp>` exposing the unchanged `native_gameboy_*` ABI for both pulses, wave RAM and noise. Apply only `friend struct NativeGameboyAccess` to the vendor header for observation and gate-only Stop, recording original/amended hashes; leave DSP, Native wrapper and WASM bridge bytes unchanged. Preserve clock conversion, stereo/gain convention, mute progression and reset's restored DMG wave pattern. Per-channel Stop retains an outer held frame below the reference clock; all-channel Stop clears it immediately.
- Add `tetorica_gameboy_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example using both pulses, an original wave-RAM triangle and noise, musical clock/divider pitch conversion, deliberate left/right phrases and fixed gain/fades. It needs no audio device, ROM, sample file or additional dependency.
- Add one shared standalone OPL-family library with `tetorica::opl` / `ym3526` / `ym3812` / `ymf262` / `y8950` aliases and matching headers. Preserve both existing Native ABIs, explicit kind selection, NEW/four-operator state and distinct Stop/reset/CSM/source-preview held semantics. Construct one selected chip/profile per handle.
- Add Y8950 writable-page integration and a dedicated memory fixture: up to 2 MiB in 512 caller-owned 4 KiB pages, logical length/revision tracking, CPU transfers, reset retention and host-owned lifetime/serialization/retirement. State access avoids data consumption/audio advancement but can propagate Y8950 status flags into IRQ; no Rust queue/COW manager/budget is imported.
- Add `tetorica_dos_opl_wav` and `tetorica_msx_audio_wav`: three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 examples. DOS demonstrates OPL/OPL2/OPL3, rhythm and a stereo four-operator pair; MSX-AUDIO combines Y8950 FM/original ADPCM-B with AY and OPLL, keeping writable sample RAM alive beyond the decoder.
- Add `tetorica::rf5c164` and `<tetorica/rf5c164.hpp>` exposing both existing primary and additional ABIs from one library. Preserve eight voices, copied 64 KiB RAM, reset retention, bank-window versus absolute upload behavior and distinct validation contracts. Primary keeps the canonical vendor core and outer clock resampling; extra keeps per-voice held contributions for immediate cancellation without advancing foreign voices.
- Add `tetorica_megacd_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example combining actual YM2612, Sega PSG and primary RF5C164. Generate an original sign-magnitude loop, avoid reserved positive `0xff`, pad loop markers for skipped bytes, and use the 12.5 MHz/384 clock with 11 fractional step bits. Keep fixed mix headroom and require no assets or audio device.
- Add the independent OKIM6258 target `tetorica::okim6258`, public `<tetorica/okim6258.hpp>` and unchanged `native_extra_okim6258_*` ABI. Preserve low-nibble-first 4-bit/12-bit decoding, a borrowed immutable sample up to 16 MiB, repeat, raw FIFO controls, rate guards and observational state. Stop/reset retain the sample binding; reset restores divider 512/pan 0 while keeping the edited clock.
- Add `tetorica_x68000_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example combining YM2151 FM at 4 MHz and original synthetic OKI percussion at 8 MHz/divider 512. Keep the borrowed sample owner alive beyond the decoder's RAII handle, with fixed mix headroom and no device or external assets.
- Add one standalone YM2610/YM2610B library with `tetorica::ym2610` / `tetorica::ym2610b` aliases and public forwarders retaining `native_ym2610b_*`. Both require explicit immutable constructor variants: four physical FM slots 1/2/4/5 or all six, with SSG and ADPCM-A/B. Preserve both profiles, dense primary ROM copies, externally owned immutable additional pages, observational status and retained Stop/reset behavior.
- Add `tetorica_neogeo_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example using one four-FM primary YM2610 with three SSG voices and original synthetic ADPCM-A/B samples. Program 256-byte ROM ranges rather than OPNA's fixed rhythm/32-byte RAM mode; no external hardware/game ROMs are required.
- Add the standalone YM2608 OPNA target `tetorica::ym2608`, public `<tetorica/ym2608.hpp>` forwarder and existing C ABI/state layouts, reusing the Native OPN provider. Preserve FM/SSG/rhythm/ADPCM-B, bounded memory copies and both reset profiles: primary clears outer output history; additional retains it. Both retain uploaded ROM/RAM, clock and source mute settings. Observational snapshots remain separate from hardware reads with side effects.
- Add `tetorica_pc98_ym2608_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example combining FM/SSG with locally generated ADPCM-A percussion and an ADPCM-B pluck. It uploads an original synthetic 8 KiB rhythm ROM and encoded sample RAM, with no external assets or hardware ROM sounds.
- Add the standalone YM2203 OPN+SSG target `tetorica::ym2203`, public `<tetorica/ym2203.hpp>` forwarder and existing `native_ym2203_*` ABI. Preserve the primary/additional constructor profiles: primary reset retains output-rate remainder/held PCM, while additional reset clears them. The shared Native OPN provider owns the helper templates without changing vendor DSP or the ABI.
- Add `tetorica_pc98_ym2203_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example using all three FM and three SSG voices, shared noise and envelope at the standard 4 MHz clock/prescaler. It uses the YM2203 SSG master/2 effective clock, mono output on both channels and no YM2608 rhythm/ADPCM assets.
- Add the standalone AY-3-8910 target `tetorica::ay8910`, public `<tetorica/ay8910.hpp>` forwarder and unchanged `native_ay8910_*` ABI, preserving three tones, shared noise/envelope, synchronous observation, retained levels, Stop/reset and audition. Keep the Native type 0 / flags 1 configuration, three-channel averaging and mono output; YM2149/type/flags selection remains outside this ABI.
- Add `tetorica_msx_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example combining real AY tones/noise/hardware envelope with an OPLL flute melody. It represents an MSX plus MSX-MUSIC sound configuration, without machine emulation or a motherboard analog mix model.
- Add the standalone YM2413 OPLL target `tetorica::ym2413`, public `<tetorica/ym2413.hpp>` forwarder and existing `native_ym2413_*` ABI, preserving the cached Native adapter's Stop/reset, observation and audition semantics. Support nine melodic channels or six FM plus five rhythm voices sharing physical channels 6–8, with mono output on both stereo channels.
- Add `tetorica_master_system_wav <output.wav>`, a three-second 48 kHz stereo PCM16 example combining OPLL's built-in piano/rhythm and Sega PSG through the real libraries. Preserve the Genesis WAV example and the shared optional example-build switch.
- Add the independent Sega PSG target `tetorica::segapsg`, forwarding `<tetorica/segapsg.hpp>` to the unchanged `native_game_gear_*` ABI, with three tone channels, noise and Game Gear stereo. Genesis/Master System output retains stereo `0xff`; no OPLL core is included.
- Add `tetorica_genesis_wav <output.wav>`, an optional offline example rendering three seconds of 48 kHz stereo PCM16 with the real YM2612 and PSG libraries, synthetic notes/noise and fixed mix headroom.
- Extend source-archive checks to require all Native fixture executables and WAV examples, validate their output, and run the same checks in the configured Native CI matrix. YM2610/YM2610B share one static library and four OPL-family kinds share another; aliases/headers include generic `opl`. The OPLL and OPL-family targets reuse the full Native template provider and unchanged support dependencies. The Game Boy header's access-only friend declaration is the sole new vendor-core amendment; ymfm bytes and WASM recipes remain unchanged.
- Add the standalone YM2151 OPM static target `tetorica::ym2151`, public `<tetorica/ym2151.hpp>` forwarder and existing C ABI, with an offline eight-channel PCM/pan, timers/status/IRQ, Stop/reset/cancellation and observation fixture. The OPM target remains independent of the separate OKIM6258 target.
- Import the Native OPM explicit-template provider fix from the same Tauri revision as the OPN fix, preserving the shared ymfm vendor bytes and WASM recipes.
- Import the Native YM2612 explicit OPN template-provider fix, retaining the original and amended provenance hashes and unchanged DSP/ABI.
- Add source-archive Release build and CTest/JavaScript CI on Windows, Linux x64/ARM64, and both Mac architectures; add a pinned-toolchain YM2612 WASM archive build/rebuild/smoke job.
- Audit CMake multi-configuration artifacts and Windows compiler paths; preserve exact source bytes across Git checkouts and include CI configuration in source releases.

## 0.1.0 — Initial SDK

- Collect source cores and existing Native C++ bridges for all 22 chips supported by Playground's additional-instance API.
- Consolidate shared ymfm sources and add chip catalogs, component licenses, origins and SHA-256 inventories.
- Add a standalone Native YM2612 CMake target and automated PCM tests. Retain other Native implementations as reference sources for subsequent integration.
- Add WASM build recipes, versioned source/WASM release archives and verification from independently extracted packages.
- Preserve existing npm and Playground Tauri dependency paths during the initial extraction; adopting SDK releases is a separate integration step.
- Document upstream adaptations, import changes and Native/WASM differences for all 22 chips and additional WASM artifacts, including six MSFA Native differences and the Game Boy Native header integration requirements.
- Document the workflow for incorporating changes verified in the application repositories and distributing pinned SDK snapshots.
- License original Tetorica code under BSD-3-Clause, retaining third-party licenses and existing explicit file-level terms.
- Include the Analyzer's unchanged MSM5205 and OKIM6295 JavaScript references, BSD notices, provenance, a standalone synthetic-data WAV example, and source-archive verification. Record them separately from Native targets and WASM recipes.
- Collect separately pinned, BSD-declared upstream MSM5205/OKIM6295/ADPCM C/C++ originals with per-file hashes. Document missing framework dependencies and omit libvgm support/player files without explicit licenses; retain the JavaScript engines and existing build targets unchanged.
